extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and developers calling PARI functions)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions: describes allowed argument types, return behavior, precision/accuracy guarantees, error conditions, and usage examples for many transcendental and arithmetic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: cos(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cosine of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcos(GEN x, long prec). (No extra notes in this chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: cosh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic cosine of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcosh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cotan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cotangent of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcotan(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: dilog(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of the dilogarithm of x, analytic continuation of the power series Li_2(x) = sum_{n>=1} x^n / n^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dilog(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: eint1(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential integral E_1(x) extended by analytic continuation from real x>0 to all complex x; if integer n is given, returns n-dimensional vector [eint1(x), ..., eint1(n*x)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN veceint1(GEN x, GEN n = NULL, long prec) and GEN eint1(GEN x, long prec). If n present require x>0; when n is present values are correct up to a bounded absolute error 10^{-n} (error controlled in absolute terms rather than relative), where n = precision(x) if x is t_REAL and defaults to realprecision otherwise. Using vector form is faster than repeated calls but less precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: erfc(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complementary error function, analytic continuation of (2/√π) ∫_x^∞ e^{-t^2} dt to all complex x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gerfc(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: eta(z, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants of Dedekind's eta function. If flag=0 returns a variant (missing q^{1/24} factor) with q depending on x; if flag!=0 returns true eta with q^{1/24} factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex x, q = exp(2iπx) and x must have positive imaginary part for the q-series; for t_PADIC or convertible power series q = x with positive valuation. Library syntax: GEN eta0(GEN z, long flag, long prec); GEN trueeta(GEN x, long prec) available (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: exp(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential of x. p-adic arguments with positive valuation are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gexp(GEN x, long prec). For t_PADIC x, GEN Qp_exp(GEN x) is also available.

rubrics_metrics.name: expm1(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return exp(x) - 1, computed accurately when real part of x is near 0 (avoids catastrophic cancellation). Only accepts real or complex arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended over exp(x)-1 when x is small: expm1 is both faster and more accurate for tiny x. Example demonstrates much smaller relative error and faster time. Library syntax: GEN gexpm1(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: gamma(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's gamma function Γ(s) for complex s; error if s is a non-positive integer (poles). For t_PADIC s evaluates the Morita p-adic gamma function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ggamma(GEN s, long prec). For t_PADIC, GEN Qp_gamma(GEN x) available. Examples show p-adic expansions and algebraic dependency detection (algdep).

rubrics_metrics.name: gammah(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gamma function evaluated at x + 1/2 (i.e., Γ(x+1/2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ggammah(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperu(a,b,x)
rubrics_metrics.description: U confluent hypergeometric function with parameters a and b; parameters a and b can be complex but current implementation requires x to be positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hyperu(GEN a, GEN b, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: incgam(s,x,{g})
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete gamma function Γ(s,x) = ∫_x^∞ t^{s-1} e^{-t} dt, extended by analytic continuation to complex x (s and x not both 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative error is bounded in terms of precision of s (accuracy of x ignored when determining output precision). Optional g argument can be Γ(s) to speed computation for small |x|. Library syntax: GEN incgam0(GEN s, GEN x, GEN g = NULL, long prec) and GEN incgam(GEN s, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: incgamc(s,x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complementary incomplete gamma function (the complementary integral from 0 to x), for complex x and s (s not a pole of Γ) and with |x|/(|s|+1) not much larger than 1 (otherwise convergence is slow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN incgamc(GEN s, GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lambertw(y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lambert W function: solution x of x e^{x} = y; described here for y>0 (principal branch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN glambertW(GEN y, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lngamma(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of log of the gamma function (log Γ(x)), analytic on C with non-positive integers removed. Can accept much larger arguments than gamma itself and can compute Taylor expansions for power series inputs whose constant term is not a pole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARI only handles regular power series (no logarithmic terms). Domain errors and warnings occur for series with zero leading term or poles; examples show use and domain error messages. Library syntax: GEN glngamma(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: log(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of natural logarithm of x ∈ C*, with imaginary part in (−π,π]; branch cut along negative real axis; p-adic arguments accepted with convention log(p)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm uses AGM-based formula for large arguments, series expansion near 1 for low accuracy. Note: for p-adic inputs exp(log(x))/x may not equal 1 but a (p−1)-th root of unity times a power of p. Library syntax: GEN glog(GEN x, long prec); GEN Qp_log(GEN x) for t_PADIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: polylog(m,x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Polylogarithm variants. If flag omitted or 0: m-th polylogarithm Li_m(x) analytic continuation of sum_{n>=1} x^n/n^m. Other flags compute modified functions (˜D_m, D_m, P_m) using Zagier's notation with specific combinations of powers of log|x| and lower polylogarithms; these satisfy functional equations f_m(1/x) = (−1)^{m−1} f_m(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses functional equations to reduce to |x|≤1, then power series or log-expansions depending on region. Library syntax: GEN polylog0(long m, GEN x, long flag, long prec); GEN gpolylog(long m, GEN x, long prec) for flag=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: psi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Digamma function ψ(x) = Γ'(x)/Γ(x) (logarithmic derivative of gamma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gpsi(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: sin(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sine of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gsin(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: sinh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic sine of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gsinh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqr(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of x. Implemented more efficiently than x*x and may increase 2-adic precision when squaring 2-adics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used whenever two identical objects are multiplied (to exploit faster squaring). Examples show precision increase for p-adic O(2^n) inputs and differences between naive multiplication and sqr. Library syntax: GEN gsqr(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrt(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of square root with Arg(sqrt(x)) ∈ (−π/2, π/2]; for negative real x returns complex with positive imaginary part. Supports t_INTMOD, t_PADIC and t_FFELT arguments where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_INTMOD and t_PADIC, returned square root (if exists) is the one whose first p-adic digit is in [0,p/2]. For other arguments behavior is undefined when square root doesn't exist. Library syntax: GEN gsqrt(GEN x, long prec); GEN Qp_sqrt(GEN x) for t_PADIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtn(x,n,{&z})
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal branch of nth root with Arg ∈ (−π/n, π/n]. Intmod prime and p-adic args allowed. Optional z returns a suitable root of unity so other roots can be recovered; if not possible z set to 0. If &z present and no root exists, returns 0 instead of raising error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior on Mod(2,7) and how to compute all roots via supplied helper sqrtnall. Library syntax: GEN gsqrtn(GEN x, GEN n, GEN *z = NULL, long prec). For t_PADIC, GEN Qp_sqrtn available.

rubrics_metrics.name: tan(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tangent of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtan(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: tanh(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolic tangent of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtanh(GEN x, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: teichmuller(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teichmüller character of p-adic number x: the unique (p−1)-th root of unity congruent to x/p^{vp(x)} modulo p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN teich(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: theta(q,z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jacobi sine theta-function θ1(z,q) = 2 q^{1/4} Σ_{n≥0} (−1)^n q^{n(n+1)} sin((2n+1)z)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN theta(GEN q, GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: thetanullk(q,k)
rubrics_metrics.description: k-th derivative at z=0 of theta(q,z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN thetanullk(GEN q, long k, long prec). GEN vecthetanullk(GEN q, long k, long prec) returns vector of odd derivatives i=1,3,...,2k-1. Variants accepting tau (q=exp(2iπ tau) ) are provided: GEN vecthetanullk_tau(GEN tau, long k, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: weber(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: One of Weber's three f functions: flag=0 returns f(x)=exp(−iπ/24) η((x+1)/2)/η(x) (with j-expressions provided), flag=1 returns f1(x)=η(x/2)/η(x), flag=2 returns f2(x)=√2 η(2x)/η(x). Various algebraic relations noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identities and relations: j expressed in terms of these f functions; identities f^8 = f1^8 + f2^8 and f f1 f2 = √2. Library syntax: GEN weber0(GEN x, long flag, long prec). Shortcuts: GEN weberf, weberf1, weberf2 available.

rubrics_metrics.name: zeta(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Riemann zeta ζ(s) = Σ_{n≥1} n^{−s} for complex s: computed using Euler-Maclaurin summation formula, except when s is integer where Bernoulli numbers or modular forms are used depending on s. For p-adic s, computes Kubota-Leopoldt p-adic zeta interpolant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gzeta(GEN s, long prec). Implementation switches algorithm based on s type (integer, p-adic), with explicit notes on interpolation properties for p-adic zeta.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic functions (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions whose natural domain is Z (or Z_{>0}); no automatic type conversions: in general only integers accepted as arguments (but alternate representations allowed like factorization or [N, fa]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integer arguments can be passed as t_MAT factorization, or t_VEC [N,fa] to reuse factorization. This is efficient when computing many arithmetic functions for the same N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic functions and the factoring engine
rubrics_metrics.description: All narrow-sense arithmetic functions (e.g., eulerphi, moebius, divisor sums) call the common factoring engine after trial division by small primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factoring engine includes Shanks SQUFOF, Pollard Rho, ECM, MPQS stages and has early-exit options for moebius and issquarefree. Uses probabilistic primality tests (ispseudoprime); user can set default(factor_proven,1) to force proven factorizations at minor speed cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders and discrete logarithm routines
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions computing orders in finite groups (ellorder, fforder, znorder) and discrete logs (elllog, fflog, znlog).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional argument specifying N (order of group) can be t_INT, t_MAT factorization, or preferred t_VEC [N, fa]. Precomputing group order/factorization once and passing it yields much better performance for repeated computations; examples show use with large primes and factor data.

rubrics_metrics.name: addprimes({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds integers in vector x (or single integer x) to a table of user-defined primes used for trial division by factor; returns the table. If x omitted returns current list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must be primes; no internal primality check performed even if factor_proven default set. Use removeprimes to delete entries. Library syntax: GEN addprimes(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bestappr(x,{B})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return rational approximation a/b to x with denominator limited by B (if provided), using continued fractions for reals; for modular/p-adic arguments performs rational modular reconstruction modulo N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If B omitted returns best approximation affordable from input accuracy. For t_INTMOD or t_PADIC does modular rational reconstruction returning unique a/b with |a|<N/2B and b ≤ B, else returns []. Applies recursively to components; if reconstruction fails for any component returns []. Examples: Pi -> 22/7, modular examples, p-adic example returning -1/3.

rubrics_metrics.name: bestapprPade(x,{B})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return rational function approximation a/b to x with degree(b) ≤ B (if provided). For series or rational-function inputs uses generalized continued fraction / extended Euclidean algorithm; for modular/p-adic performs rational modular reconstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If B omitted returns best affordable approximation. If reconstruction fails returns []. Applies recursively to components. Examples include Pade approximants for power series and modular examples (returns [] when not possible). Library syntax: GEN bestapprPade(GEN x, long B).

rubrics_metrics.name: bezout(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for gcdext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcdext0(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: bigomega(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of prime divisors of |x| counted with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: factor(392) shows exponents and bigomega(392)=5, while omega(392)=2 (without multiplicity). Library syntax: long bigomega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: binomial(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binomial coefficient: y must be integer, x can be any PARI object; returns binomial(x,y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN binomial(GEN x, long y). Additional helpers: GEN binomialuu(ulong n, ulong k) and GEN vecbinome(long n) returning row of binomial coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinese(x,{y})
rubrics_metrics.description: Chinese remainder combination: given intmods or polmods x and y returns z in same residue class as both if possible. If y omitted and x vector, applies recursively to vector components yielding residue common to all components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For polynomial arguments in same variable chinese applied coefficient-wise; care advised for differing degrees (high-degree terms copied verbatim); suggestion to convert polynomials to vectors of same length first. Behavior: chinese(x,x)=x always. Library syntax: GEN chinese(GEN x, GEN y = NULL); GEN chinese1(GEN x) also available. Examples demonstrate mixing Mod types and vectorized use.

rubrics_metrics.name: content(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute gcd of all coefficients of x (polynomial, power series, vector/matrix); for scalar x returns absolute value if rational, else 1 or x depending on inexact/exact input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of rational function is ratio of numerator and denominator contents. In recursive structures, matrix/vector coefficients use their content for gcd. Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN content(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: contfrac(x,{b},{nmax})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return row vector of partial quotients of continued fraction expansion of x; result [a0,...,an] means x ≈ a0 + 1/(a1 + ... + 1/an).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nmax limits number of partial quotients; if omitted stops at last significant quotient. Can accept rational functions or power series. If vector b supplied numerators equal coefficients of b leading to generalized continued fraction expansion. Examples show contfrac(Pi) and contfrac(Pi,,3). Deprecated hack: if b integer, old meaning. Library syntax: GEN contfrac0(GEN x, GEN b = NULL, long nmax). Other related functions: GEN gboundcf, GEN gcf, GEN gcf2.

rubrics_metrics.name: contfracpnqn(x,{n=-1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector or one-row matrix of partial quotients [a0,...,an], returns 2x2 matrix [pn, pn-1; qn, qn-1] with pn/qn the convergent. If matrix with two rows gives generalized continued fraction result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n ≥ 0 returns all convergents up to pn/qn. Applies regardless of vector length if too small. Examples show contfracpnqn(contfrac(Pi,20),3). Library syntax: GEN contfracpnqn(GEN x, long n); GEN pnqn(GEN x) for n=-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: core(n,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integer n written as n = d f^2 with d squarefree, returns d; if flag!=0 returns [d,f]. Convention: core(0,1) returns [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN core0(GEN n, long flag). Also GEN core(GEN n) and GEN core2(GEN n) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: coredisc(n,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the unique fundamental discriminant d such that n = d f^2, with d a fundamental discriminant (t ≡1 mod4 or 4t≡8,12 mod16 and t squarefree). If flag!=0 return [d,f]. Convention coredisc(0,1) returns [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: quaddisc(n) returns same value and accepts rationals. Note on parity of f (integer or half-integer) depending on n mod 4. Library syntax: GEN coredisc0(GEN n, long flag); GEN coredisc(GEN n) (flag=0) and GEN coredisc2(GEN n) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: dirdiv(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vectors x and y representing Dirichlet series (possibly different lengths), computes quotient x/y as Dirichlet series vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dirdiv(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: direuler(p=a,b,expr,{c})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Dirichlet series associated to Euler product given by polynomial/rational expr as p ranges over primes from a to b; expr(X) interpreted as local factor expr(p^{-s}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is vector of coefficients; optional c to return only first c coefficients. Example given computing sigma function from appropriate local factor. Library syntax (C-level): direuler(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: dirmul(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vectors x and y representing Dirichlet series, compute their Dirichlet convolution product as a vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product length is minimum of #x*v(y) and #y*v(x) where v(x) first non-zero coefficient index. Examples given. Library syntax: GEN dirmul(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: divisors(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return row vector of divisors of x. For integers returns positive divisors in increasing order. Factorization of x can be supplied to speed computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition given: divisors are products of irreducible factors raised to powers (no negative exponents). Library syntax: GEN divisors(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: eulerphi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's totient function φ(|x|) = |(Z/xZ)^*|. By convention φ(0):=2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfies znstar(n).no = eulerphi(n) for all n∈Z. Library syntax: GEN eulerphi(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: factor(x,{lim})
rubrics_metrics.description: General factorization for rationals (incl. integers), Gaussian integers, or rational functions/polynomials. Returns two-column matrix: irreducibles and exponents. By convention 0 factored as 0^1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over Q and Q(i) result uses pseudoprimes (ispseudoprime) — factors ≤ 2^64 are genuine primes. Use isprime to prove primality or set default factor_proven. Optional lim (t_INT) restricts to prime factors p < lim (non-negative); remaining factor may be composite. Routine uses trial division and perfect power tests; for large lim use factorint or factorint/other specialized routines. Many domain-specific notes: factoring domains detected and supported (Q,R,C,Qp,finite fields, number fields) with algorithms like van Hoeij's over Q for polynomials. Clarifies behavior for polynomial factoring (content discarded) and recommends explicit variant factormod/factorff/factorpadic/nffactor/polroots for clarity/performance. Library syntax: GEN gp_factor0(GEN x, GEN lim = NULL) for gp interface; use GEN factor(GEN x) or GEN boundfact(GEN x, ulong lim) at C-level.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorback(f,{e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconstruct the factored object from a factorization. If e present, uses exponent vector e; if f vector and e omitted assumes exponents 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization. Examples: factor(12) then factorback returns 12; factorback([2,3],[2,1]) returns 12. Library syntax: GEN factorback2(GEN f, GEN e = NULL); GEN factorback(GEN f) also available.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorcantor(x,p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor polynomial x modulo prime p using distinct degree plus Cantor-Zassenhaus algorithm. Coefficients must be compatible with Z/pZ. Result is 2-column matrix of irreducible polynomials and exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only degrees needed use factormod(x,p,1). Note factormod may be faster. Library syntax: GEN factcantor(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorff(x,{p},{a})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor polynomial x in finite field F_q defined by irreducible polynomial a over F_p (field extension); coefficients must be compatible with Z/pZ. Returns two-column matrix of factors and exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all coefficients are in F_p a faster algorithm is used. Either a or p can be omitted if x has t_FFELT coefficients. Examples show usage and error when not enough info to determine base field; advises easier syntax using ffgen and shows readable outputs. Library syntax: GEN factorff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factorial of x: expression x! gives integer result, while factorial(x) returns real number approximation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mpfactr(long x, long prec) for real factorial; GEN mpfact(long x) returns x! as t_INT.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint(x,{flag=0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor integer x into product of pseudoprimes using combination of Shanks SQUFOF, Pollard Rho (Brent), Lenstra's ECM (Montgomery), MPQS, and pure-power search. Output is two-column matrix of prime divisors and exponents. By convention 0 -> 0^1, 1 -> empty factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default output may contain unproven 'primes' > 2^64 (pass through probabilistic BPSW test); use isprime or set default factor_proven to 1 to guarantee primes. Optional flag bits: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first ECM stage, 4 avoid Rho and SQUFOF, 8 don't run final ECM. Warning that probabilistic tests are used and composites might not be detected (no known counterexamples). Debugging and flag settings available; invited to watch internals via gp debug parameter. Library syntax: GEN factorint(GEN x, long flag).
